audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Sabbath healing, hardness of heart, Pharisees/Herodians plot, crowds, appointment of the Twelve, Beelzebul controversy, binding the strong one, Spirit warning, and family redefinition around doing the Divine will.

verses.restored: He entered again into the synagogue, and a man with a withered hand was there.

familiar.text: And he entered again into the synagogue; and there was a man there which had a withered hand.

modern.text: Once again Jesus entered the synagogue, and a man with a withered hand was there.

original.text: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν πάλιν ⸀εἰς συναγωγήν, καὶ ἦν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπος ἐξηραμμένην ἔχων τὴν χεῖρα.

verses.restored: They were watching him closely, whether he would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse him.

familiar.text: And they watched him, whether he would heal him on the sabbath day; that they might accuse him.

modern.text: In order to accuse Jesus, they were watching to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.

original.text: καὶ παρετήρουν αὐτὸν εἰ τοῖς σάββασιν θεραπεύσει αὐτόν, ἵνα ⸀κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: He said to the man with the withered hand, Rise into the middle.

familiar.text: And he saith unto the man which had the withered hand, Stand forth.

modern.text: Then Jesus said to the man with the withered hand, “Stand up among us.”

original.text: καὶ λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τῷ ⸂τὴν χεῖρα ἔχοντι ξηράν⸃· ⸀Ἔγειρε εἰς τὸ μέσον.

verses.restored: He said to them, Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save life/soul or to kill? But they were silent.

familiar.text: And he saith unto them, Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil? to save life, or to kill? But they held their peace.

modern.text: And He asked them, “Which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?” But they were silent.

original.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν ⸀ἀγαθοποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι, ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ἀποκτεῖναι; οἱ δὲ ἐσιώπων.

verses.restored: Looking around at them with anger, grieved at the hardness of their heart, he said to the man, Stretch out your hand. He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.

familiar.text: And when he had looked round about on them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their hearts, he saith unto the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it out: and his hand was restored whole as the other.

modern.text: Jesus looked around at them with anger and sorrow at their hardness of heart. Then He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” So he stretched it out, and it was restored.

original.text: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος αὐτοὺς μετʼ ὀργῆς, συλλυπούμενος ἐπὶ τῇ πωρώσει τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν, λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ· Ἔκτεινον τὴν ⸀χεῖρα· καὶ ἐξέτεινεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ ⸀αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: The Pharisees went out and immediately took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.

familiar.text: And the Pharisees went forth, and straightway took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.

modern.text: At this, the Pharisees went out and began plotting with the Herodians how they might kill Jesus. Jesus Heals the Multitudes (Matthew 4:23–25; Luke 6:17–19)

original.text: καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ⸀εὐθὺς μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν συμβούλιον ⸀ἐδίδουν κατʼ αὐτοῦ ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν.

verses.restored: Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea, and a great multitude from Galilee followed, and from Judea,

familiar.text: But Jesus withdrew himself with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judaea,

modern.text: So Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea, accompanied by a large crowd from Galilee, Judea,

original.text: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ⸂μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἀνεχώρησεν⸃ πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ πολὺ πλῆθος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ⸀ἠκολούθησεν, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας

verses.restored: from Jerusalem, Idumea, beyond the Jordan, and around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing all he was doing, came to him.

familiar.text: And from Jerusalem, and from Idumaea, and from beyond Jordan; and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, when they had heard what great things he did, came unto him.

modern.text: Jerusalem, Idumea, the region beyond the Jordan, and the vicinity of Tyre and Sidon. The large crowd came to Him when they heard what great things He was doing.

original.text: καὶ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰδουμαίας ⸀καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου ⸁καὶ περὶ Τύρον καὶ Σιδῶνα, πλῆθος πολύ, ⸀ἀκούοντες ὅσα ⸀ἐποίει ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτόν.

verses.restored: He told his disciples that a little boat should be ready for him because of the crowd, so they would not crush him.

familiar.text: And he spake to his disciples, that a small ship should wait on him because of the multitude, lest they should throng him.

modern.text: Jesus asked His disciples to have a boat ready for Him so that the crowd would not crush Him.

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα πλοιάριον προσκαρτερῇ αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἵνα μὴ θλίβωσιν αὐτόν·

verses.restored: For he healed many, so that all who had afflictions pressed upon him to touch him.

familiar.text: For he had healed many; insomuch that they pressed upon him for to touch him, as many as had plagues.

modern.text: For He had healed so many that all who had diseases were pressing forward to touch Him.

original.text: πολλοὺς γὰρ ἐθεράπευσεν, ὥστε ἐπιπίπτειν αὐτῷ ἵνα αὐτοῦ ἅψωνται ὅσοι εἶχον μάστιγας.

verses.restored: Whenever the unclean spirits saw him, they fell before him and cried out, saying, You are the Son of the Divine.

familiar.text: And unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, saying, Thou art the Son of God.

modern.text: And when the unclean spirits saw Him, they fell down before Him and cried out, “You are the Son of God!”

original.text: καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα, ὅταν αὐτὸν ⸂ἐθεώρουν, προσέπιπτον⸃ αὐτῷ καὶ ⸀ἔκραζον ⸀λέγοντα ὅτι Σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: He strictly warned them many times that they should not make him known.

familiar.text: And he straitly charged them that they should not make him known.

modern.text: But He warned them sternly not to make Him known. The Twelve Apostles (Matthew 10:1–4; Luke 6:12–16)

original.text: καὶ πολλὰ ἐπετίμα αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ ⸂αὐτὸν φανερὸν⸃ ⸀ποιήσωσιν.

verses.restored: He went up into the mountain and called those whom he wanted, and they came to him.

familiar.text: And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.

modern.text: Then Jesus went up on the mountain and called for those He wanted, and they came to Him.

original.text: Καὶ ἀναβαίνει εἰς τὸ ὄρος καὶ προσκαλεῖται οὓς ἤθελεν αὐτός, καὶ ἀπῆλθον πρὸς αὐτόν.

verses.restored: He appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles/sent ones, so that they might be with him and so that he might send them to proclaim,

familiar.text: And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,

modern.text: He appointed twelve of them, whom He designated as apostles, to accompany Him, to be sent out to preach,

original.text: καὶ ἐποίησεν ⸀δώδεκα, ἵνα ὦσιν μετʼ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἵνα ἀποστέλλῃ αὐτοὺς κηρύσσειν

verses.restored: and to have authority to cast out unclean spirits.

familiar.text: And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils:

modern.text: and to have authority to drive out demons.

original.text: καὶ ἔχειν ⸀ἐξουσίαν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια·

verses.restored: He appointed the twelve: Simon, to whom he gave the name Peter;

familiar.text: And Simon he surnamed Peter;

modern.text: These are the twelve He appointed: Simon (whom He named Peter),

original.text: καὶ ⸂ἐποίησεν τοὺς δώδεκα, καὶ⸃ ἐπέθηκεν ⸂ὄνομα τῷ Σίμωνι⸃ Πέτρον,

verses.restored: James son of Zebedee and John the brother of James, to whom he gave the name Boanerges, that is, Sons of Thunder;

familiar.text: And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:

modern.text: James son of Zebedee and his brother John (whom He named Boanerges, meaning “Sons of Thunder”),

original.text: καὶ Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν τοῦ Ἰακώβου (καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτοῖς ⸀ὀνόματα Βοανηργές, ὅ ἐστιν Υἱοὶ Βροντῆς),

verses.restored: Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Cananaean/Zealot,

familiar.text: And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,

modern.text: Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot,

original.text: καὶ Ἀνδρέαν καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν καὶ Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ Θαδδαῖον καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν ⸀Καναναῖον

verses.restored: and Judas Iscariot, who also handed him over. Then he came into a house.

familiar.text: And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.

modern.text: and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus. A House Divided (Matthew 12:22–30; Luke 11:14–23)

original.text: καὶ Ἰούδαν ⸀Ἰσκαριώθ, ὃς καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: The crowd gathered again, so that they were not even able to eat bread.

familiar.text: And the multitude cometh together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.

modern.text: Then Jesus went home, and once again a crowd gathered, so that He and His disciples could not even eat.

original.text: Καὶ ⸀ἔρχεται εἰς οἶκον· καὶ συνέρχεται πάλιν ⸀ὁ ὄχλος, ὥστε μὴ δύνασθαι αὐτοὺς ⸀μηδὲ ἄρτον φαγεῖν.

verses.restored: When those near him heard, they went out to seize him, for they were saying, He is beside himself.

familiar.text: And when his friends heard of it, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself.

modern.text: When His family heard about this, they went out to take custody of Him, saying, “He is out of His mind.”

original.text: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ παρʼ αὐτοῦ ἐξῆλθον κρατῆσαι αὐτόν, ἔλεγον γὰρ ὅτι ἐξέστη.

verses.restored: The scribes who came down from Jerusalem were saying, He has Beelzebul, and, By the ruler of the unclean spirits he casts out the spirits.

familiar.text: And the scribes which came down from Jerusalem said, He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casteth he out devils.

modern.text: And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, “He is possessed by Beelzebul, ” and, “By the prince of the demons He drives out demons.”

original.text: καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς οἱ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καταβάντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Βεελζεβοὺλ ἔχει καὶ ὅτι ἐν τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια.

verses.restored: Calling them to him, he spoke to them in parables: How can Satan/adversary cast out Satan/adversary?

familiar.text: And he called them unto him, and said unto them in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan?

modern.text: So Jesus called them together and began to speak to them in parables: “How can Satan drive out Satan?

original.text: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐν παραβολαῖς ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Πῶς δύναται Σατανᾶς Σατανᾶν ἐκβάλλειν;

verses.restored: If a reign is divided against itself, that reign is not able to stand.

familiar.text: And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.

modern.text: If a kingdom is divided against itself, it cannot stand.

original.text: καὶ ἐὰν βασιλεία ἐφʼ ἑαυτὴν μερισθῇ, οὐ δύναται σταθῆναι ἡ βασιλεία ἐκείνη·

verses.restored: If a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.

familiar.text: And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand.

modern.text: If a house is divided against itself, it cannot stand.

original.text: καὶ ἐὰν οἰκία ἐφʼ ἑαυτὴν μερισθῇ, οὐ ⸀δυνήσεται ⸂ἡ οἰκία ἐκείνη σταθῆναι⸃·

verses.restored: If the adversary has risen against himself and is divided, he is not able to stand but has an end.

familiar.text: And if Satan rise up against himself, and be divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.

modern.text: And if Satan is divided and rises against himself, he cannot stand; his end has come.

original.text: καὶ εἰ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἀνέστη ἐφʼ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ⸀ἐμερίσθη, οὐ δύναται ⸀στῆναι ἀλλὰ τέλος ἔχει.

verses.restored: But no one is able to enter the strong one's house and plunder his goods unless first he binds the strong one; then he will plunder his house.

familiar.text: No man can enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he will first bind the strong man; and then he will spoil his house.

modern.text: Indeed, no one can enter a strong man’s house to steal his possessions unless he first ties up the strong man. Then he can plunder his house. The Unpardonable Sin (Matthew 12:31–32)

original.text: ⸂ἀλλʼ οὐδεὶς δύναται⸃ ⸂εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ εἰσελθὼν τὰ σκεύη⸃ αὐτοῦ διαρπάσαι ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον τὸν ἰσχυρὸν δήσῃ, καὶ τότε τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ ⸀διαρπάσει.

verses.restored: Amen, I say to you: all things will be released for the children of humanity, the sins/misalignments and whatever blasphemies they speak.

familiar.text: Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:

modern.text: Truly I tell you, the sons of men will be forgiven all sins and blasphemies, as many as they utter.

original.text: Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πάντα ἀφεθήσεται ⸂τοῖς υἱοῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων, τὰ ἁμαρτήματα⸃ καὶ ⸂αἱ βλασφημίαι ὅσα ἐὰν⸃ βλασφημήσωσιν·

verses.restored: But whoever blasphemes against the holy Spirit does not have release into the age, but is held by age-long sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation:

modern.text: But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven; he is guilty of eternal sin.”

original.text: ὃς δʼ ἂν βλασφημήσῃ εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, οὐκ ἔχει ἄφεσιν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἀλλὰ ἔνοχός ἐστιν αἰωνίου ⸀ἁμαρτήματος.

verses.restored: because they were saying, He has an unclean spirit.

familiar.text: Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.

modern.text: Jesus made this statement because they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.” Jesus’ Mother and Brothers (Matthew 12:46–50; Luke 8:19–21)

original.text: ὅτι ἔλεγον· Πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον ἔχει.

verses.restored: His mother and his brothers came, and standing outside they sent to him, calling him.

familiar.text: There came then his brethren and his mother, and, standing without, sent unto him, calling him.

modern.text: Then Jesus’ mother and brothers came and stood outside. They sent someone in to summon Him,

original.text: ⸂Καὶ ἔρχονται⸃ ⸂ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ⸃ καὶ ἔξω ⸀στήκοντες ἀπέστειλαν πρὸς αὐτὸν ⸀καλοῦντες αὐτόν.

verses.restored: A crowd was sitting around him, and they said to him, Look, your mother and your brothers and sisters are outside seeking you.

familiar.text: And the multitude sat about him, and they said unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren without seek for thee.

modern.text: and a crowd was sitting around Him. “Look,” He was told, “Your mother and brothers are outside, asking for You.”

original.text: καὶ ἐκάθητο ⸂περὶ αὐτὸν ὄχλος⸃, ⸂καὶ λέγουσιν⸃ αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί ⸀σου ἔξω ζητοῦσίν σε.

verses.restored: He answered them, Who are my mother and my brothers?

familiar.text: And he answered them, saying, Who is my mother, or my brethren?

modern.text: But Jesus replied, “Who are My mother and My brothers?”

original.text: καὶ ⸂ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτοῖς λέγει⸃· Τίς ἐστιν ἡ μήτηρ μου ⸀ἢ οἱ ἀδελφοί ⸀μου;

verses.restored: Looking around at those sitting in a circle around him, he said, Look, my mother and my brothers.

familiar.text: And he looked round about on them which sat about him, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren!

modern.text: Looking at those seated in a circle around Him, He said, “Here are My mother and My brothers!

original.text: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος ⸂τοὺς περὶ αὐτὸν κύκλῳ⸃ καθημένους λέγει· Ἴδε ἡ μήτηρ μου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί μου·

verses.restored: Whoever does the will of the Divine, this one is my brother and sister and mother.

familiar.text: For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.

modern.text: For whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother.”

original.text: ὃς ⸀γὰρ ἂν ποιήσῃ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, οὗτος ἀδελφός μου καὶ ⸀ἀδελφὴ καὶ μήτηρ ἐστίν.
